html:
Canada is a federal country in northern North America, the second largest in the world by area. It was formed by Confederation in 1867 and gained full legal independence from Britain step by step, ending in 1982.

Before Europeans, the land was home to many First Nations and the Inuit. The French founded New France along the St Lawrence, with Quebec City in 1608, and lived largely from the fur trade. The British, with the Hudson's Bay Company, traded further north. Britain took New France in 1763. After the American Revolution, thousands of Loyalists moved north, adding an English-speaking population beside the French one.

Confederation on 1 July 1867 joined Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick into the Dominion of Canada, partly from fear of the United States after its Civil War. The new country soon stretched to the Pacific, and a railway across the continent was finished in 1885. Settlement of the prairies pushed aside the Métis and First Nations, whose children were later forced into residential schools, a wrong the country is still reckoning with.

Canada's independence grew in stages rather than by revolution:

  • It fought in both world wars, and its own sacrifices built a separate national identity.
  • The Statute of Westminster in 1931 gave it full control of its laws.
  • In 1982 it took full control of its constitution, adding a Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

The British monarch is still head of state. Quebec's French-speaking identity has shaped its politics, with independence referendums lost in 1980 and 1995.
sum: Canada is a federal country in northern North America, the second largest in the world by area. It was formed by Confederation in 1867 and gained full legal independence from Britain step by step, ending in 1982.
